{{Quote|Send Rogues Ten and Eleven to Station 3-8.|General Carlist Rieekan|<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
'''Tarrin Datch''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] who served with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. A product of the Datch family&ndash;owned [[Realspace/Legends|space]] [[City/Legends|city]] [[Pellezara station]] in the [[Duro system/Legends|Duro system]], Tarrin became a skilled flier while helping to manage the many cargo [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]] of the [[Space station/Legends|space station's]] clients. Datch joined the Rebellion as a seventeen-[[Standard year/Legends|year]]-old in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], after helping a fugitive [[Unidentified Alliance freighter|Alliance freighter]] carrying stolen [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] cargo and the Rebel [[Alliance Special Operations/Legends|special operative]] [[Jan Ors]], seeking refuge at Pellezara station, escape Imperial pursuit and reach its destination. His value to the Rebellion's cause came in the dual ability to pilot both starfighters and the Alliance's dilapidated cargo [[Transport/Legends|transports]], and Datch's talents earned him a position with the elite [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]], under the command of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], as [[Rogue Ten/Legends|Rogue Ten]]. Datch fought most notably during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] at the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] with Rogue Group, participating in the [[Evac Rearguard Action 101|delaying action]] that bought time for the transports and personnel of [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] to evacuate the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. He later piloted the [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]] [[Thon's Orchard/Legends|''Thon's Orchard'']] safely through the Imperial [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].

==Biography==
===Early years===
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]]<ref name="RS" /> Tarrin Datch was a native of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Duro/Legends|Duro]].<ref name="Warfare" /> He was born in [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]] on [[Pellezara station]], a floating [[Realspace/Legends|space]] [[City/Legends|city]] in the [[Duro system/Legends|Duro system]] owned by his [[Tarrin Datch's mother|mother]] and [[Tarrin Datch's father|father]] that serviced large [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]] delivering supplies to Duro. Growing up, his siblings included at least two brothers and one [[Tarrin Datch's sister|sister]]. In addition to servicing [[Starship/Legends|starships]], Datch's parents frequently put on stunt shows for the waiting freighter [[Captain/Legends|captains]] to alleviate boredom. Datch, already a gifted [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] by the age of twelve [[Galactic Standard Calendar|standard years]], assisted in these flight shows along with his siblings. These performances involved daring maneuvers with modified [[Cargo tug/Legends|cargo tugs]] and [[cargo-flitter]]s in crowded areas with free-floating [[service bay]]s and [[Cargo container/Legends|cargo containers]], which created a visually spectacular show.<ref name="GG3" />

When he wasn't performing complex loops and rolls in between [[container ring]]s and [[repair grid]]s, Datch was typically tasked with helping to move freighters into parking slots while their captains relaxed. He was once grounded for three [[Standard week/Legends|standard weeks]] by his father, literally, being assigned to handle traffic control and resupply, after he attempted a miniature [[Koiogran turn]] in a [[Bulk freighter/Legends|bulk freighter]], taking out a dozen [[beacon pod]]s in the process&mdash;though the freighter captain never found out.<ref name="GG3" />

===Joining the Rebellion===
In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], when Datch was seventeen, he was replacing the [[gravity disk]]s in the deckplates of a docked [[Unidentified Alliance freighter|freighter]] that was, unknown to him and the Datch family, carrying stolen [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Fuel slug/Legends|fuel slugs]] bound for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. While dismantling one of the ship's particularly stubborn plates, he discovered a hidden compartment holding a wounded [[Gender/Legends|woman]], who identified herself as [[Jan Ors]]. Her right [[Limb/Legends|leg]] was stricken with a strange injury sustained in the jungles of [[Oulanne/Legends|Oulanne]]. Datch was both terrified and captivated. In her delirium, Ors revealed the freighter's Rebel ties to Datch.<ref name="GG3" />

The Empire soon arrived at Duro, in hot pursuit of the stolen cargo. The freighter's crew had disembarked for the [[Space station/Legends|station]] to find medical supplies for Ors, and Datch was the only pilot aboard. He knew he could not allow the valuable [[Fuel/Legends|fuel]] slugs to fall back into Imperial hands, so he took control of the freighter and broke away from Pellezara's main docking tower, heading for open space. The Rebels still in the station could only watch in horror as their freighter left them stranded, being followed closely by an Imperial [[Gamma-class assault shuttle/Legends|''Gamma''-class assault shuttle]]. Datch steered the Rebel [[Transport/Legends|transport]] toward the heart of the station's heavy traffic, weaving as though he was piloting a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]]. The Imperial ship could barely keep up, inadvertently scraping its hull against stationary [[lighter]]s and space tugs. Datch was able to reach open space and engage the ship's [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], leaving Pellezara behind for an outlying-[[Star system/Legends|system]] [[Unidentified outer-system station|station]] he often used as a stunt range.<ref name="GG3" />

There, in the outer station's well-equipped medical center, Datch helped to stabilize Ors's condition. He knew they could not return to Pellezara, and how badly the Rebellion needed the fuel they carried. Ors gave him the coordinates of a secret [[Dantooine base/Legends|Rebel base]] on the planet [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], and the two soon left for Rebel sanctuary. At Dantooine the two separated, with Ors going off on other secret missions, while Datch began training as a [[Rebel pilot/Legends|Rebel fighter pilot]]. Although he missed his family, Datch knew he could not risk involving them in the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], for their safety.<ref name="GG3" />

===Fighting the Empire===
{{Quote|This thing's headed straight for the base&hellip;We're gonna have to take a crack at it.''"<br />"''&hellip;I'll have Rogue Ten and Rogue Eleven make an attack run&hellip;''"<br />"''&hellip;There's no time for that. Besides, if it sees the snowspeeders, it'll know we're here for sure&hellip;|General Carlist Rieekan and Han Solo discuss Datch possibly attacking the Viper probe droid|<ref name="ESBRadio script">[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''The Empire Strikes Back'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref>}}
Datch's experience flying cargo freighters while growing up on Pellezara station was a great asset to his new allies, with the Rebellion frequently finding itself short of both ships and capable pilots. With his valuable abilities, Datch's shifting role found him alternating between flying starfighters and piloting the Rebels' dilapidated freighters and transport vessels.<ref name="GG3" />
{{GameMechanics|legends=1}}
Sometime following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], and his recruitment into the Rebel Alliance, Datch partook in a skirmish against at least one [[TIE pilot|Imperial pilot]]. Datch was defeated in the fight, but managed to escape alive in his crippled [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]]. Datch also participated in battles between Rebel and Imperial forces in the [[Naboo system/Legends|Naboo]], [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo]], [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian]], [[Dantooine system/Legends|Dantooine]], and [[Karthakk system]]s during the Galactic Civil War. These battles involved an Imperial [[Lancer-class frigate/Legends|Lancer-class frigate]] being pitted against a Rebel [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]], with numerous starfighters aiding in the defense or offense of the system.<ref name="SWG" />
{{Endgame}}
At some point during his service with the Rebel Alliance, Datch was assigned to the nascent [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Group]], an elite starfighter [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]] formed around two of the survivors of the Battle of Yavin&mdash;[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]]. He flew under the [[Callsign/Legends|call sign]] [[Rogue Ten/Legends|Rogue Ten]] and soon earned the title of starfighter [[Ace/Legends|ace]].<ref name="GG3" /> While with the Rogues, Datch developed friendships with fellow pilots Skywalker, Antilles, and [[Wes Janson/Legends|Wes Janson]].<ref name="Essential Guide">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>

[[File:SnowspeederPatrol-SW39.png|thumb|left|255px|Tarrin Datch and Rogue Eleven, Tenk Lenso, were dispatched to Echo Station 3-8 to investigate the probe droid.]]
By [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], four [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after joining the Rebellion, Datch was assigned to the secret [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on the remote ice world of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] with the rest of the Rogues. His duties on Hoth included patrolling the planet's icy wastes in the base's modified [[T-47 airspeeder/Legends|T-47 airspeeders]], dubbed [[Snowspeeder/Legends|snowspeeders]]. When an Imperial reconnaissance [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droid]] discovered Echo Base in 3 ABY, Datch, along with [[Rogue Eleven/Legends|Rogue Eleven]], [[Tenk Lenso]], was among the first pilots dispatched by base commander [[General/Legends|General]] [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]] to respond to the threat.<ref name="GG3" /><ref name="ESB" /><ref name="ESB novel">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref><ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> He and Lenso were instructed to fly over [[Echo Station 3-8]] at low altitude and to expect trouble.<ref name="ESBRadio script" /> They also transported [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] to the site of the [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droid]].<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Solo and Chewbacca tracked down the probe soon thereafter, warning Rieekan that it might have detected the base's [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]]. Rieekan intended to order Datch and Lenso on an attack run for the probe, but Solo dismissed the idea, claiming there was no time and that the sight of snowspeeders flying overhead would alert the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] to their presence. Instead, he announced that he and Chewbacca would handle the probe themselves.<ref name="ESBRadio script" /> The probe droid's discovery of Echo Base would soon throw the twenty-one-year-old Datch headlong into the fray of one of the war's most significant battles.<ref name="GG3" />

===Battle of Hoth===
{{Quote|Yeah! Transport Away!|Derek Klivian, elated after the escape of Datch and the ''Thon's Orchard''|<ref name="GG3" />}}
[[File:TarrinDatchSnowspeeder.png|thumb|right|250px|Tarrin Datch attacks General Maximilian Veers' AT-AT during the Battle of Hoth.]]
When the Empire invaded Echo Base during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], Datch flew one of the base's [[Airspeeder/Legends|snowspeeders]] with Rogue Group.<ref name="GG3" /> [[Hosh Hune]] served as Datch's gunner during the battle.<ref name="Warfare" /> They were given the monumental task of [[Evac Rearguard Action 101|delaying]] the advance of several Imperial [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transport]] [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] long enough to buy sufficient time for the base's vulnerable transports and personnel to escape the planet.<ref name="GG3" /> Early in the engagement, Datch made a strafing run directly over the command section of General [[Maximilian Veers/Legends|Maximilian Veers]]' lead AT-AT, [[Blizzard 1/Legends|Blizzard 1]], inflicting little damage.<ref name="TCG">{{TCG|set=The Empire Strikes Back|link=https://swtcg.com/Content/Images/Cards/ESB/Snowspeeder_Rogue_Ten.webp?v=2|cardname=Snowspeeder Rogue Ten}}</ref> Realizing that Rogue Group's [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] were too weak for the AT-ATs' [[Armor/Legends|armor]], Skywalker ordered the use of the snowspeeders' [[Power harpoon launcher|harpoon and tow cables]] to trip the massive machines' legs.<ref name="ESB" />

Datch's speeder was shot down by Imperial fire late in the battle,<ref name="RS" /> and Hosh Hune was killed in action.<ref name="Warfare" /> However Skywalker rescued Datch before a group of three [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|All Terrain Scout Transports]] could descend on his position.<ref name="RS" /> Ultimately, Datch's airspeeder was salvaged.<ref name="Warfare" /> Datch safely returned to Echo Base, where he reconvened with Antilles and the final Rebel remnants on the [[South Ridge/Legends|South Slope]] preparing to evacuate the planet. He and Antilles waited for Skywalker, who had also been shot down, to join them before lifting off.<ref name="Millennium Falcon Pursuit">{{ESBRadio|The Millennium Falcon Pursuit}}</ref>

[[File:Rogue_Ten_RS_Game.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Tarrin Datch, near his downed snowspeeder]]
Datch was once again pressed into dual piloting service. He was tasked with piloting the [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]] [[Thon's Orchard/Legends|''Thon's Orchard'']] off Hoth, one of the final transports to evacuate the planet. However, his job did not end with simply flying the ship free of the besieged base. Waiting in Hoth's [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] to intercept the fleeing Rebel ships was a [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] line of [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]]&mdash;[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] personal [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]].<ref name="GG3" /> To complicate matters, the base's [[V-150 Planet Defender/Legends|v-150 anti-orbital ion cannon]] was no longer operational and unable to provide covering fire for the vulnerable ''Thon's Orchard''.<ref name="Millennium Falcon Pursuit" />

Flying escort for Datch's transport were two T-65 X-wing starfighters piloted by Skywalker and Antilles, and a [[BTL-S3 Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL-S3 Y-wing starfighter]] piloted by fellow Rogue [[Derek Klivian/Legends|Derek Klivian]] with Janson riding along as [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]]. The ''Thon's Orchard''{{'s}} flight path was directly blocked by one of the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]]. Antilles and Klivian executed the fanciful maneuver known as the [[Tallon split]], in conjunction with a surprise attack from Skywalker from below the transport, to help Datch and the ''Thon's Orchard'' escape into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] and rejoin the Rebels at their predetermined [[Haven (rendezvous point)|rendezvous point]] beyond the edge of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="GG3" /><ref name="Essential Guide" /> Skywalker did not make the jump with the other Rebels, making what seemed to be a strange excuse that he wanted to keep an eye on another nearby Star Destroyer group. In reality, he was charting a separate course to the [[Dagobah system/Legends|Dagobah system]]; Tarrin and the others arrived at the rendezvous without their commander.<ref name="Millennium Falcon Pursuit" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|We're just gonna have to trust to luck!''"<br />"''Luck, right! Get to your ships, you meatballs! We're lifting off!|Tarrin Datch and Luke Skywalker, discussing the impending Hoth blockade run|<ref name="Millennium Falcon Pursuit" />}}
One of Tarrin Datch's virtues included an empathy for family values, assisting his family in both the maintenance of Pellezara station and the flight shows his parents put on for their customers. After piloting the fugitive Rebel freighter carrying Jan Ors away from his family's station and joining the Rebellion's cause, he knew better than to return to Pellezara or to involve his family in any way with his affairs, for the danger it would cause them.<ref name="GG3" />

Datch also carried with him a penchant for daredevilry, risking the ships of Pellezara's clients in order to perform perilous maneuvers. He even used another remote space station as a stunt range. Although his youthful innocence initially betrayed feelings of trepidation at learning who and what the [[Alliance Special Operations/Legends|Rebel agent]] Jan Ors was, his risk-taking nature soon clicked in to give him the brazen confidence to defy the Empire.<ref name="GG3" />

As an extension of his daring nature, Datch was more than willing to place his stock in luck in the face of overwhelming danger. While conferring with Skywalker and Antilles regarding Echo Base's inoperable v-150 [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]]&mdash;neutralized during the battle&mdash;Datch was eager to test their luck in taking on the Imperial blockade without the protection of the ion cannon's covering fire.<ref name="Millennium Falcon Pursuit" />

Aside from his starfighter and starship transport piloting abilities, Datch was appropriately skilled in the maintenance of such vehicles, as well as airspeeder [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] operation and repair, and starship [[Astrogation/Legends|astrogation]]. He could also hold his own as a starship gunner.<ref name="GG3" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Notable appearances===
[[File:RebelPilotHoth9-2.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Datch in ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]
The character named "Tarrin" first appeared in "[[The Millennium Falcon Pursuit]]," the fifth episode of the [[1983]] [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|radio adaptation]] of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']].<ref name="Millennium Falcon Pursuit" /> He was voiced by [[Sam McMurray]].<ref name="Encyclopedia of Radio">{{BookCite|author=Christopher H. Sterling|title=Encyclopedia of Radio|number=vol. 3|publisher=[[Wikipedia:Routledge|Routledge]]|date=2004|isbn=9781135456498|link=https://books.google.com/books?id=-UeveLMilioC&dq=Frank%20Mankiewicz%20star%20wars&pg=PA2206 }}</ref> Datch's last name and biographical details were first established in the [[1996]] second edition of the [[West End Games]] sourcebook [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'']], which was also the first source to connect the "Tarrin" radio adaptation character with the identity of "Rogue Ten" from the film.<ref name="GG3" /> The character was originally created by [[Brian Daley]] for the radio drama's script after story conferences concluded in [[November]] [[1981]]; the script was not published until the release of ''[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization]]'' in [[1995]].<ref name="ESBRadio script" /> In 2013, an [[Rogues Gallery (department)|article]] in [[Star Wars Insider 146|''Star Wars Insider'' 146]] linked Datch's name to one of the unnamed pilots seen being briefed by Princess Leia during ''The Empire Strikes Back''.

Datch's actions at the Battle of Hoth were later expanded and first visually represented in the [[1998]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]. [[Paul Amendt]] provided the voice of "Rogue Ten" for the game, though it should be noted that the Rogue Ten character speaks during the game's "[[Escape from Fest]]" level, which is not necessarily confirmed as corresponding to the actual Datch character.<ref name="RS" />

Through the art of "[[retroactive continuity]]," the Tarrin Datch character is now [[canon]]ically established to have first appeared in ''[[Star Wars]]'' media in two separate publications&mdash;the [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]] of ''The Empire Strikes Back'', written by [[Donald F. Glut]], and the illustrated children's book ''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]'', adapted by [[Shep Steneman]], both of which were released simultaneously on [[April 12]], [[1980]], just prior to the film's [[May]] theatrical release.<ref name="ESB novel" /><ref name="ESB Storybook">''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]''</ref> The following paragraphs detail the Datch character's unique canonical development.

The "Snowspeeder Rogue Ten" card, from the November [[2003]] [[The Empire Strikes Back (TCG)|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] expansion set of the [[Wizards of the Coast]] ''[[Star Wars Trading Card Game]]'', identifies a snowspeeder that makes an attack run on the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] of General Veers' AT-AT during the Battle of Hoth, as seen in the film, as Rogue Ten&mdash;Tarrin Datch<ref name="TCG" />&mdash;thus retconning ''The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization, which originally included a description of this scene, as one of the character's two "first" appearances.<ref name="ESB novel" /> Notably, this scene is also described in the [[2004]] [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back (junior novelization)|junior novelization]] of ''The Empire Strikes Back'', written by [[Ryder Windham]], which instead identifies the attacking snowspeeder pilot as Luke Skywalker.<ref name="ESB junior novelization">[[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' junior novelization]]</ref>

Datch's involvement in responding to the Imperial probe droid outside of Echo Base just prior to the Battle of Hoth have been expanded on in several sources to include additional scenes not included in the original film. Specifically, ''The Empire Strikes Back Storybook'' makes mention of a group of snowspeeders that delivers Han Solo and Chewbacca to the location of the probe droid.<ref name="ESB Storybook" /> Notably, the [[September]] 1980 [[Star Wars (1977)|''Marvel Star Wars'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] adaptation of ''The Empire Strikes Back'', [[Star Wars (1977) 39|''Star Wars'' (1977) 39]], also includes a panel in which a snowspeeder patrol delivers Solo and Chewbacca to the probe.<ref name="Marvel">[[Star Wars (1977) 39|''Star Wars'' (1977) 39]]</ref> The substance of this scene, first detailed in ''The Empire Strikes Back Storybook'', was referenced in the [[2008]] release of ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', under the "Rogue Eleven" entry, confirming that Datch and Tenk Lenso, specifically, transported Solo and Chewbacca to the probe,<ref name="CSWE" /> thus retconning ''The Empire Strikes Back Storybook'' as the character's other "first" appearance, albeit indirectly, in ''Star Wars'' media.<ref name="ESB Storybook" /> ''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio adaptation and the radio drama's original script, ''The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization'', likewise include unique dialogue for the scene, in which General Rieekan considers ordering Datch and Rogue Eleven to attack the probe themselves.<ref name="ESBRadio script" /><ref name="Millennium Falcon Pursuit" />

[[File:TarrinDatchGCW.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Datch in ''Star Wars Galaxies'']]
In the [[2003]] [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|MMORPG]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']], Tarrin Datch was added to the [[Star Wars video games|game]] as a [[Wikipedia:Non-player character|non-player character]] in [[W:c:swg:Game Update 20|Game Update 20]]. Imperial players who requested [[W:c:swg:Tier|Tier 7]] [[W:c:swg:Destroy Duty Missions|Duty Missions]] from certain [[Space station/Legends|space stations]] had a chance to battle an [[W:c:swg:Ace Pilot System|elite Rebel pilot]] during the mission's boss stage. One of these pilots could be Tarrin Datch. If the player defeated Tarrin Datch, the Rebel was not destroyed. Instead, a message was displayed to the player, indicating that they successfully defeated the pilot. The player then received a [[W:c:swg:Collection|collection]] icon which added up to award a [[W:c:swg:Badges|badge]] if they succeeded in destroying all ten of the elite Rebel pilots. However, elite Rebel pilots could also be found flying in various space battles, which took place in the [[Naboo system/Legends|Naboo]], [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo]], [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian]], [[Dantooine system/Legends|Dantooine]], and [[Karthakk system]]s. Because Tarrin Datch only appeared in the space portion of ''Star Wars Galaxies'', originally added with the [[Star Wars Galaxies: Jump to Lightspeed|''Jump to Lightspeed'']] expansion pack, he could normally only be seen inside his respective [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]]. However, a comm display could appear during the battle, displaying Tarrin Datch's face. In addition, the collection icon depicted Tarrin Datch's physical appearance. Although players could choose not to participate in any of the battles or collections connected to Tarrin Datch, this article assumes 100% game completion.<ref name="SWG" />

===Inconsistencies===
{{Quote|Luke, uh, my scopes are picking up two Imperial Star Destroyers.''"<br />"''I see 'em too, Tarrin, but they're too far back to give us any trouble now.|Tarrin Datch and Wedge Antilles, in an excerpt from ''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio adaptation|<ref name="Millennium Falcon Pursuit" />}}
Several sources include a description of the Hoth blockade run made by Datch, inspired from the original script of ''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio adaptation.<ref name="ESBRadio script" /> However, the actual audio recording of the radio drama differs substantially from the script and subsequent sources. Rather than Datch's starfighter escort engaging a Star Destroyer attempting to intercept his transport, Datch and the fighters only detect two Star Destroyers too spread out from the battle to pose a threat, and simply slip through the blockade and enter hyperspace without trouble. Additionally, the transport Datch pilots away from Hoth in the radio adaptation is intended to be the final evacuation transport,<ref name="Millennium Falcon Pursuit" /><ref name="BTM" /> though this is later contradicted by the short story ''[[Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM]]'', which identifies the GR-75 medium transport [[Bright Hope/Legends|''Bright Hope'']] as the final transport to leave, a ship that fails to escape the Imperial blockade.<ref name="OPF">{{StoryCite|story=Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref>

According to the novel ''[[X-Wing: Isard's Revenge]]'', Wedge Antilles identifies the GR-75 medium transport [[Dutyfree/Legends|''Dutyfree'']] as the ship Datch pilots off Hoth.<ref name="Isard">''[[X-Wing: Isard's Revenge]]''</ref> ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'' repeats the ''Dutyfree'' designation and omits any reference to the ''Thon's Orchard''.<ref name="CSWE" />

Datch appears in the [[2006]] [[Wikipedia:Personal computer|PC]] game ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'' among the Rogue Squadron starfighter unit. However, it should be noted that Datch and the Rogue Squadron unit only appear in "Galactic Conquest" and "Skirmish" modes, which are not considered part of the game's canonical storyline. Additionally, the game misspells Datch's first name as "Tarrub."<ref name="EAW">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref>
